item.title: Russia marched into Huliaipole in December. Now it can’t march out.
item.description: Ukrainian advances in the southeast are taking the pressure off Zaporizhzhia city and its 700,000 pre-war residents.

item.title: NATO in talks to bring more Ukrainian know-how to allied air defense
item.description: Goal to be able to take down 95% of all air threats

item.title: Taking Ukraine’s lessons seriously, Netherlands becomes first NATO member to integrate drones across all combat formations
item.description: The Dutch military is recruiting up to 1,200 personnel to staff units embedded throughout the army, not concentrated in specialist formations.

item.title: Rosneft’s classified document recommended smoke screens against GPS-guided drones — and the same document explains why that’s useless
item.description: Every barrier in the document also uses shallow foundations to dodge permit requirements — a structural choice the presentation explicitly flags as its own kill switch. Putin's simultaneous PMC-arming law is Moscow's admission the engineering fixes aren't enough.

item.title: Mesh networked ‘smart mines’ under development by Poland, Estonia, Ukraine
item.description: Likely to be used along the borders of Russia and its allies

item.title: Ukraine’s anti-corruption court upholds 6-year term for ex-tax chief in gas scheme
item.description: Appeals chamber confirms sentence nine years on, with the clock nearly out.

item.title: Drones caused 96% of Russia’s losses in March – 34,000 troops killed or wounded
item.description: Zelenskyy's tally puts unmanned systems far ahead of every other weapon combined.

item.title: Ukraine may be using Libya as launchpad for Mediterranean strikes on Russian shadow fleet – RFI
item.description: RFI investigation finds more than 200 Ukrainian officers and technical specialists based across three Libyan sites, with Tripoli's approval – and direct Mediterranean access.

item.title: Another Russian national off the US sanctions list — this time a former finance minister who ran Russia’s third-largest bank
item.description: ikhail Zadornov, sanctioned in 2022 for heading Otkritie Bank, successfully petitioned OFAC for removal. The US Treasury insists it reflects no broader policy change, but the delisting follows similar moves in late March.

item.title: Stoltenberg offered Russia NATO troop withdrawals from the Baltic region — without asking the Baltic states
item.description: A new memoir by the former NATO Secretary General reveals he proposed discussing troop withdrawals that the alliance's Baltic members had not consented to—and knew nothing about.

item.title: Magyar’s Birds took out a Buk-M1, wiped fuel stocks, and hit logistics in Luhansk – all in one night
item.description: A wave of coordinated Ukrainian drone strikes across three days also destroyed Orion drones in Crimea and a Buk-M3 in Luhansk Oblast.

item.title: Egypt was Russia’s biggest stolen-grain customer. Now it pledges to buy Ukrainian wheat instead.
item.description: Cairo pledged to stop accepting Russian-supplied grain from occupied Ukrainian territories after a call with Zelenskyy – just as Putin pitched Egypt as a hub for Russian commodities.

item.title: Russo-Ukrainian war, day 1500: Ukraine may be striking Russia’s shadow fleet from Libya — and Egypt just switched sides on stolen grain
item.description: An RFI investigation places more than 200 Ukrainian military specialists at three Libyan sites with Mediterranean access, on the same day Cairo pledged to stop buying Russian-supplied grain from occupied Ukrainian territory and purchase Ukrainian wheat instead.

item.title: Ukraine’s top defense market segments doubled to $6.8 Billion in 2025
item.description: “Ukraine’s defense-technology sector is rapidly evolving into one of the most dynamic and scalable components of the country’s industrial economy.”

item.title: Trump wants out of NATO. Good. Let him go.
item.description: Not an anti-American position—a pro-European one.
